problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}xy\,dx+y\,dy+z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the curve $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j+{t}^{3}\,k$ for $t\in [3,5]?$
worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=t,\,y(t)={t}^{2},\,z(t)={t}^{3}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})\,k \\  & =\,i+2t\,j+3{t}^{2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}xy\,dx+y\,dy+z\,dz & ={\int }_{3}^{5}xy\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}(xy\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}{t}^{3}\cdot (1)+{t}^{2}\cdot (2t)+{t}^{3}\cdot (3{t}^{2})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}3{t}^{5}+3{t}^{3}\,dt \\  & =3{\int }_{3}^{5}{t}^{5}+{t}^{3}\,dt\end{aligned}
$$
